Today, I am going to explain to you the entire production process of this pair of Parisian tank shoes. You can see the complete picture on my A-stand. ## Overview of the Shoes This pair of shoes is made by MD. All the plates and materials used are visible here. You can see that this block is very broken; basically, it's all done in MD. The entire shape is adjusted in MD. Then in JB, I used plastic dust to create a texture material in SD. Finally, we come to this B-stand, where I made a simple assembly and added more details. The details of this pair of shoes are more in-depth, and it took some time to complete. ## Introduction to the Process Because today's time is relatively tight, I may not cover too many points of knowledge. The main focus will be on the overall production process of this pair of shoes. Generally, when it comes to writing, the first step is to collect materials. There are still a lot of materials for this pair of shoes available on Taobao and B-stand, but there are not many high-definition pictures, and relatively few clear pictures. I've been searching for a long time, and I found quite a few. ### Material Collection I personally do a lot of writing, and I like to use Taobao because it is very easy to collect pictures compared to using Google or Pinterest. When searching for reference pictures, I usually look for details that are clearly displayed and have a clearer structure. Videos that rotate 360 degrees are particularly useful as they allow you to understand line structures and how to render the picture at the end. ### Complexity of the Shoe Design When dealing with shoes, especially this particular shoe, the sole's spring structure is quite complicated. Initially, I spent two days finding a reference picture to think about how to insert it. Inside, it has some insertion structures, and every part has a mutual insertion between each part. Finding references for the bottom of the shoe was particularly time-consuming, as very few pictures are available. ## Step-by-Step Production Process ### Step 1: Shoe Hanger and Shoulder Strings Let's get started. The first step involves getting a shoe hanger and shoulder strings, similar to mine. Our main function is to hang up this. Here, I'll turn it off first. It's easy to make a shoe hanger—just take your model and create a rough outline according to the style of the shoe. ### Step 2: Creating the Shoe Sole I prepared two essential components: the shoe sole and the shoe upper. The shoe sole is a little more complicated, so let me show you how to make it in MD. I prepared a model of the shoe sole, all made in MD. 1. **Modeling the Shoe Sole**: Start by creating a large piece for the bottom of the shoe. You can do this in any direction, generally flat. 2. **Adjusting the Shape**: After modeling, you can use semi-transparent mode to draw the inner line, cut it off, and finish the bottom of the shoe. 3. **Curving the Sole**: Use the inner line to adjust the curvature to resemble leather shoes. ### Step 3: Detailing the Upper of the Shoe After the sole is complete, I moved on to the upper part of the shoe. I made a lining seam on the side, taking care to ensure that the edge is not directly on the side but rather on the top or bottom, depending on the style of the shoe. ### Step 4: Reference and Texture When making shoes, finding a reference picture is crucial for achieving an accurate design. Even though it is difficult to find a perfect reference, you can use a general model as a base. The methods are largely the same whether you are making high-heeled shoes or sneakers. ### Step 5: Final Assembly After completing the shoe base, I began assembling the shoe. At this stage, I made sure to keep all the parts separate to avoid merging them, which could complicate the process. ## Challenges in the Production Process During the production, I faced several challenges, such as ensuring that the shoe structure didn't collapse and managing the details for a more realistic finish. Any small adjustments I made were crucial to the overall design, especially in achieving natural folds and creases. ## Conclusion This live stream covered the production process of the Balenciaga Spring shoes using Marvelous Designer 2024. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Thank you for your attention, and I look forward to sharing more insights in future sessions.
